where M has σησάμα [sesame], some copies σεισάμα, on which see L. Dindorf in Thes. vol. 7 p. 199. "That the true reading is Σισάμνα [Sisamna], and the others are due to scribes straying to σήσαμον [sesame] or σεισ, is shown by the variety of spelling in Herodotus (5, 25. 7, 66.) for the name Σισάμνης [Sisamnes]. But Σεισάμης ὁ Μύσιος [Seisames the Mysian] at v. 322 seems to be a different person, unless this too should be written with 1, if Σισάμνης [Sisamnes] is correctly spelled."
